claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The dual-phase structure can combine a soft, ductile FCC phase with a hard B2 phase.
L12 may constitute the hard phase in the starting lamellar structure.
Dislocation pile-ups occur near internal phase boundaries in the untreated alloy.
Boundary-associated dislocation pile-ups generate local stress concentrations, microcracking, and brittle or catastrophic failure during room-temperature tension.
A phase-selective annealing treatment can selectively recrystallize the ductile phase while substantially preserving the hard phase.
Annealing at approximately 700°C for a short duration under argon is suitable for producing the proposed phase-selective recrystallization.
Room-temperature quasi-static tensile testing at a strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1 is applicable for assessing the treatment.
The treatment will produce a refined, recrystallized ductile phase embedded within or arranged alongside a retained hard-phase framework.
The recrystallized ductile phase will have fewer and more uniformly distributed grain boundaries while retaining a fine lamellar arrangement.
Recovery and partial recrystallization redistribute and reduce accumulated dislocations at phase interfaces.
Reducing interfacial dislocation accumulation alleviates pile-ups, local stress concentrations, and microcrack nucleation.
The retained hard phase continues to impede dislocation motion and thereby preserves high strength.
Phase-selectively recrystallized eutectic high-entropy alloys can exhibit high uniform elongation together with high strength.
The proposed annealed alloy will have greater uniform tensile ductility than the untreated starting alloy without losing, and potentially while increasing, yield and ultimate tensile strength.
Excessive coarsening or recrystallization of the hard phase would reduce strength, whereas insufficient treatment would fail to relieve pile-ups.
The optimal treatment parameters and the quantitative ductility and strength changes in the specific starting alloy remain uncertain and require experimental validation.

contradictions.description: The intervention is said to refine the ductile-phase grain structure, which ordinarily increases grain-boundary area or density, while the structural mediator simultaneously describes the refined phase as having reduced grain boundaries. The intended distinction may be elimination of weak boundaries, but that is not stated consistently.
